hypothesis.statement: Remove the mult else-arm surplus instruction by a means OTHER than a statement-shape respell of the if/else-if/else chain, which is now dead four ways. The target hoists `lfs f4,sItemFloorRadius` to +0x64, BEFORE the gold/ramp comparison is even computed, and lets the `gold > ramp` test fall through to the merge. The one construct class not yet tried is making the else value a value the compiler must materialise unconditionally for a REASON OTHER THAN the chain -- e.g. because `sItemFloorRadius` is already loaded for the immediately following `if (power < ...) power = sItemFloorRadius;` clamp, so hoisting that clamp's load above the chain (or sharing one named f32 local between the else arm and the clamp) could supply the early lfs without an added copy. Once ours reaches 923 in that block, apply `item->data[6] = (s8)state;` -- already measured to land the extsb -- to return to 924 with one more structural row closed.
